video_title: Is Robinhood Chain Reigniting Crypto’s Retail Economy?
gist: The Blockworks research panel argues that memecoins paired against tokenized equities on Robin Hood chain are a genuinely new AMM primitive that solves the cold-start liquidity problem for onchain stocks, and that the resulting activity has flipped Base on network REV and L2 gross profit while pushing Robin Hood chain to ~50% of all Uniswap volume. They pair this with a bull case on FOMO as crypto's breakout social-trading app, a breakdown of Ethena's buyback and fee-switch overhaul, and a read that DAT mNAVs are about to reclaim 1x.

themes.theme: Memecoin–equity pairing as a new AMM primitive

insights.claim: The core economic function of an AMM pool is to bind the value of two assets together, which is why memecoins have historically been paired against a chain's base asset — buying $500 of a Salana memecoin in 2024 was an indirect $500 bid for SOL, mechanically propagating memecoin demand into the L1 token.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Explains why L1/L2 tokens rally reflexively during memecoin manias, and gives a template for judging which asset actually captures a trenches cycle's flow.
insights.quote: If you buy $500 of a memecoin, you're indirectly buying $500 of Soul, right? So that drives it up.

insights.claim: Pairing a memecoin against the tokenized equity it thematically imitates — the largest example being an artificial-dog AI memecoin paired with Nvidia — is a strictly better design than pairing against ETH or SOL, because the quote asset now has direct exposure to the same narrative the memecoin is trading.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Predicts a wave of thematically-matched memecoin/equity pairs; the quote-asset choice becomes a screenable signal for which stocks receive reflexive onchain bid.
insights.quote: It's artificial enu AI. It's paired with Nvidia, right?

insights.claim: Robin Hood chain won this meta specifically because Robin Hood is itself the issuer of the stock tokens, giving traders implicit trust that the tokenized equity leg will not be rugged — a trust premium competing stock-token venues cannot easily replicate.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Issuer identity, not chain tech, is the moat in tokenized equities — favors regulated brokerages over pure-crypto issuers when assessing which venue captures the flow.
insights.quote: Robin Hood is just like a good environment for these stock tokens to come on chain because Robin Hood is the issuer behind them.

insights.claim: Memecoin pairings solve the cold-start problem for tokenized equities: there is almost no organic onchain demand to trade stocks that people can already trade in a brokerage account, so a price-insensitive memecoin buyer is what bootstraps the first $1–10 million of onchain equity liquidity.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Gives stock-token issuers a concrete go-to-market: seed a memecoin pair rather than wait for institutional demand — and a leading indicator for which issuer's supply grows next.
insights.quote: You need like a price insensitive buyer and like memecoins are perfect for that.

insights.claim: There is no observed natural demand for buying tokenized stocks onchain, so the open question is whether onchain equities are a real market or purely a casino wrapper with the memecoin as the only working use case so far.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A direct challenge to the tokenized-RWA bull case: underwrite these venues on speculative velocity, not on an assumed migration of real equity trading onchain.
insights.quote: I've not met any single person who wants to buy a tokenized stock onchain

insights.claim: Providing liquidity to a memecoin/equity pool is defensible even for a rational investor: it is a barbell where the LP position mechanically rebalances out of the winning memecoin into the safer equity leg, producing a concave payoff with exposure to both, and current pool APYs on these stock pairs run into the thousands of percent.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Frames LPing these pools as a structured product rather than pure degeneracy — a fee-harvest trade with automatic de-risking, though it needs irrational counterparties to persist.
insights.quote: you're effectively doing like uh a concave portfolio you're dinging out of the winner very slowly into the into the into the smaller one over time

themes.theme: Tokenized-equity plumbing: premiums, depegs and whitelisted mints

insights.claim: A memecoin called boner paired against heavily-shorted HIMS forced onchain tokenized HIMS to trade at a large premium to the offchain stock, and that premium is itself the incentive that pulls market makers into minting new tokenized supply — visible in Robin Hood chain's total tokenized-equity supply inflecting sharply upward.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Onchain-vs-offchain equity premiums are a real-time gauge of memecoin demand and a forward indicator of tokenized-supply growth on a chain.

insights.claim: The worst observed depeg was the memecoin Cinema paired with AMC, where the onchain tokenized equity traded at roughly 100x the real stock price, meaning the memecoin's price action never transmitted into the actual equity market and instead just created a larger arbitrage gap.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Quality of market making is the binding constraint on this narrative going mainstream; wide depegs signal an arb opportunity but also that the 'memecoins move stocks' story is not yet real.
insights.quote: the meme one that had the craziest like deping or whatever was uh Cinema, which was like paired with AMC and it traded like nearly like 100x or something crazy like that to like what the actual price was

insights.claim: Robin Hood does not mint or burn its own stock tokens — whitelisted approved market makers such as Rialto do — and because minting and burning halt when the equity market is closed, weekend memecoin runs force onchain equity prices to dislocate with no arbitrage release valve.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Creates a recurring, calendar-driven arb: dislocations build over weekends and compress at the Monday open, which is tradeable in both the equity token and the paired memecoin.
insights.quote: when the market's closed, these tokens can't be mint or burned

insights.claim: The reflexivity runs both ways — when the equity market reopens and arbitrageurs mint tokenized supply to close the premium, the paired memecoin itself corrects meaningfully, as happened over the most recent weekend.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Memecoins in equity pairs carry a structural Monday-morning drawdown risk that is absent from SOL- or ETH-paired memecoins.

insights.claim: The memecoin-driven short-squeeze narrative is mechanically implausible on a name like HIMS — the onchain buying is barely a dent against the stock's market cap and short interest — so the real test is whether much lower-market-cap equities can be brought onchain and what the legal process for that looks like.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Watch for small/micro-cap listings on tokenized-equity venues — that, not large caps, is where an onchain squeeze narrative could actually go viral and mainstream.
insights.quote: if you just look at like the sheer market cap of the HIM stock itself and the amount of short interest on this stock it's like barely a dent

insights.claim: Onchain tokenized-equity volumes are roughly a thousand times smaller than offchain equity volumes, so genuine onchain equity trading is a long-dated outcome that likely requires a full memecoin/tokenized-equity supercycle to first put the initial one-to-ten billion dollars of stock supply onchain.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Sets expectations: treat current tokenized-equity metrics as bootstrap-phase, and size the opportunity off supply growth rather than volume parity with TradFi.

insights.claim: Onchain equity volume will only rival TradFi when users start treating onchain accounts as their savings accounts, and the two credible distribution catalysts for that are Robin Hood and Coinbase, helped by the convenience of trading crypto, stocks and gold on one platform.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Points the tokenization trade at consumer distribution platforms rather than at infrastructure protocols; also notes real existing demand from users without access to traditional brokers.

themes.theme: Robin Hood chain economics versus HOOD equity

insights.claim: Robin Hood Network's real economic value cleared over $2 million in a single day, with consecutive daily increases above $1 million in the prior week, flipping Base to make it one of the top-earning networks in crypto.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: A hard fundamental datapoint anchoring the Robin Hood chain thesis and the relative-value case against Base-linked exposure.

insights.claim: Robin Hood's crypto segment generated roughly $100 million in revenue last quarter, so a sustained $2 million REV day would annualize to about $180 million per quarter — nearly doubling the crypto business — while even a much more conservative $500k/day would add roughly $45 million a quarter, about half the current crypto line.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Gives an explicit revenue bridge from daily onchain REV to quarterly segment revenue — the arithmetic to size how much of the chain the street should be capitalizing.
insights.quote: I believe last quarter Robin Hood crypto revenue was 100 million for the entire quarter

insights.claim: Ryan expects the current $2 million REV/day run-rate to fade absent a full-blown bull market, comparing it to the 2024 Salana frenzy when $2 million REV days were unremarkable and sustained for months.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Frames the sustainability question as the single variable that decides whether HOOD re-rates on crypto; track REV persistence, not the peak print.
insights.quote: would be shocked if it maintains like 2 million REV a day

insights.claim: Crypto is now under 10% of Robin Hood's overall business — prediction markets alone did roughly $150 million last quarter — so even a tripling of crypto revenue does not materially move the consolidated P&L, and Robin Hood should not be underwritten as a crypto company.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Cools the reflexive 'buy HOOD for the chain' trade; the cleaner expressions of Robin Hood chain success are the ecosystem tokens, not the equity.
insights.quote: Robin Hood really isn't a crypto company anymore.

insights.claim: Crypto has been the one Robin Hood business unit that stopped growing over the past year, so if chain activity holds the segment could 2–3x this quarter and restore a crypto growth narrative investors had written off — the actual mechanism by which the stock would pop.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: The re-rating path for HOOD is narrative reversal on a stagnant segment, not incremental dollars — makes next quarter's crypto revenue print the key event.

themes.theme: L2 share war: Robin Hood chain flips Base

insights.claim: Leadership in tokenized-equity spot volume has changed hands twice in three months: Salana cleared over 90% of it in June, BNB chain took the lead through July and August, and Robin Hood chain now clears over 50% of onchain tokenized-equity spot volume.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Tokenized-equity share is proving highly transient — evidence that distribution, not incumbency, decides the venue, and a warning against extrapolating any leader's share.

insights.claim: Robin Hood chain went from zero to roughly 95% of daily L2 gross profit, flipping Base by multiples after Base had held in excess of 80% of that metric.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: The starkest single metric validating the chain-plus-distribution thesis and the long Robin Hood chain / short Base ecosystem pair trade.

insights.claim: Base is not out of the race — Mark thinks it fumbled by chasing social and creator-content coins instead of leaning harder into DeFi, and is now correcting with Bitcoin-backed mortgages, Morpho vaults and Aerodrome integration, but its single biggest catalyst would be issuing a token, which he views as inevitable despite disliking it.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A Coinbase/Base token is the identified catalyst to watch; the prior chart pattern of Base-versus-Arbitrum flipping suggests these leads are recoverable.
insights.quote: I don't think coin you can count them out yet. I think it's way too early for that.

insights.claim: REV is a biased scoreboard for chains: savings, cashback and neobank use cases generate real user value but nothing like the transaction intensity of a trenches casino, so Base's lower REV does not mean it is losing — closing the REV gap would require Base to manufacture an onchain wealth effect, most plausibly by teasing a token.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Corrects a common analytical error — do not rank chains on REV alone when their use cases have structurally different transaction velocity.
insights.quote: a successful chain may not necessarily translate to like as high RV numbers as we're seeing for Robin Hood

themes.theme: Uniswap's Robin Hood windfall and the V4 hook gap

insights.claim: Robin Hood chain just crossed 50% of Uniswap's total volume (48%+ the day prior), and in roughly a decade there has never been a single week in which Ethereum accounted for less than half of Uniswap volume — a first that is now expected to happen this week.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A decade-long structural first: Uniswap's demand base is migrating off Ethereum, which changes where UNI's fee accrual and Ethereum's DEX-driven activity come from.
insights.quote: there has never been a single week where the more than half of the volume from unis swap is not on Ethereum

insights.claim: Uniswap turned on the V3 and V4 fee switch on Robin Hood chain within about 15 days of the chain launching, converting that volume directly into token burns — daily UNI burns are now crossing roughly 500k.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Speed of fee-switch activation is what converts a volume windfall into token value accrual — a repeatable checklist item when assessing which DEX benefits from a new chain.
insights.quote: just within 15 days in they were like okay yeah let's turn on the V3 V4 fee switch

insights.claim: With value now accruing to the token, UNI has become the cleanest liquid-fund proxy for the Robin Hood chain thesis — the same slot pump occupies for a degen-season bet — with near-term catalysts from meme/equity pairs and V4 hooks, while the long-run thesis hinges on Uniswap dominating tokenized-equity volume, which Kunal rates roughly 50/50 given hyperlquid and other competition.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A concrete liquid-token expression of the Robin Hood chain trade, with an explicit distinction between the strong short-term catalyst and the contested long-term thesis.

insights.claim: Hook-based pools account for only about 2–5% of Uniswap V4 volume — vanilla pools are 95–98% — even though V4 has already flipped V3 in total volume, with V4's growth driven mainly by stablecoin swaps that win aggregator flow via lower, more flexible fees than V3 allows.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Quantifies the untapped upside: the hook design space that everyone cites as V4's differentiator is barely contributing volume yet, so hook adoption is a distinct, still-unpriced growth vector.
insights.quote: if you look at like hook volume and you split it up by or V4 volume you split it up by hook and vanilla vanilla volumes are actually like I think 98 or like 95% of them

insights.claim: V4 hooks remain underrated by both the market and retail users, and the builder design space around them is still vastly underexplored — the panel expects the most interesting recent onchain innovation, including stone-broker style mechanisms, to keep concentrating there.
insights.speaker: guest (Blockworks research panelist)
insights.so_what: Identifies hooks as a category where early builder attention is likely mispriced relative to eventual volume share.
insights.quote: I do think V4 hooks are underrated.

insights.claim: Many of the top gas-consuming contracts on Robin Hood chain are routers sitting in front of Uniswap, capturing application revenue because they own distribution and control of the end user rather than the liquidity.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Value in this stack is being split between the AMM and the interfaces that own the user — a reminder to check who captures the fee before assuming the protocol does.

themes.theme: FOMO and social trading as the retail onramp

insights.claim: FOMO printed a new daily all-time high in net revenue with active traders rising steadily, and its practical utility extends beyond trading to discovery and due diligence on small-cap onchain tokens.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: FOMO's revenue trajectory is a direct read on whether the retail onchain revival is broadening beyond a single chain's memecoin cycle.

insights.claim: FOMO is the first team since Friend.tech in 2023 to crack crypto-social, and crucially it is building a genuinely new social network rather than gamifying existing crypto-social mechanics — which is why its user base, not its feature set, is the moat against Pump's competing app.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Sets the right competitive metric for the social-trading category: measure user-base composition and retention rather than feature parity.
insights.quote: the most important feature of any social media network is the user base

insights.claim: FOMO's decisive advantage is that it collapsed crypto's onboarding funnel — no Coinbase account, bank link, separate wallet download or bridging step; a user signs up with Apple ID and Apple Pay and trades immediately, with the crypto layer abstracted away.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Onboarding friction, not blockspace, has been the binding constraint on retail crypto growth — apps that remove it should capture disproportionate new-user share.
insights.quote: no longer do you have to create a Coinbase account, load your bank account in, buy crypto, then download a separate wallet, bridge or send your money to that wallet

insights.claim: FOMO's roughly 100,000 users are demonstrably not just ported-over crypto Twitter: Ryan has about 70,000 FOMO followers versus a smaller X following, and multiple accounts have thousands of FOMO followers with under a thousand on X, indicating the app is reaching a trading cohort that CT never captured.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Evidence the retail pie is genuinely growing rather than rotating — the strongest argument that a 10x or 100x in FOMO's user base is plausible.
insights.quote: I have like 70,000 followers on FOMO now, which is significantly higher than my ex account.

insights.claim: FOMO materially upgrades small-cap due diligence: where a block explorer returns only hexadecimal addresses for a token's top 10 holders, on FOMO roughly 50–80% of those same holders are identified, with their trading history, stated thesis and likely X identity attached.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: A concrete new research workflow — deanonymized holder bases turn wallet analysis into attributable conviction analysis for onchain small caps.

insights.claim: For FOMO to become durable rather than cyclical, it must broaden past memecoins — currently about half its volume is memecoin trading and the other half SOL/stable swaps that are memecoin-adjacent — and become the venue where serious investors publish positions and theses in real time, the way a Chanos-style report or an inverse-Cramer basket moves markets today.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Volume mix is the key health metric for FOMO — a shift away from memecoin-linked volume would signal it is becoming financial infrastructure rather than a cycle app.

insights.claim: Creator or copy-trading vaults built on top of FOMO — a hyperlquid-style deposit into a named trader's strategy — would deconstruct the fund model, letting top alpha generators run capital without a fund structure or accredited-investor gating, with the main risk being that copied traders use their followers as exit liquidity.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: An identified product gap nobody has built yet; whoever ships automated creator vaults on a social-trading base could capture the retail asset-management layer.
insights.quote: these top like alpha generators don't need to like have funds anymore

insights.claim: The social-alpha repricing effect already exists in far larger markets — a Chanos public report repriced a security 40% the next day and an AI-stock name repriced 100% in a week after Leopold Aschenbrenner followed it on X — which is why replicating it as an onchain structured product should work.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Anchors the copy-trading thesis in observed TradFi behavior rather than crypto novelty, supporting the case that social-signal products have durable demand.

insights.claim: ENA shipped a dense week of announcements — an early-investor buyback, a token transparency framework filing, fee-switch expansion to equity perpetual basis trades, the sunsetting of Hyena, and neobank news — which the panel reads as deliberately clearing the deck rather than accidental clustering.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A checklist of the specific catalysts already in the price — useful for judging what incremental news is left to drive the token.

insights.claim: The announcement timing is a deliberate risk-on positioning play: ENA has always been the risk-on proxy because basis yields and TVL rise as markets heat up, and the buyback and utility news specifically neutralize the two standing investor objections — no token utility and early-investor overhang.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Explains ENA's beta profile and why the token became structurally more investable heading into a bull regime — a template for reading other tokens' catalyst sequencing.

insights.claim: Ethena's buybacks only switch on when sUSDe APY exceeds 6% and scale up with TVL, but current yields are only around 4.5% approaching 5%, so the announced buyback is not yet live and getting there likely needs crypto basis to widen — RWA basis trades are unlikely to be scalable enough near-term to bridge the gap.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: The 6% sUSDe APY threshold is the single tripwire to monitor — below it the buyback narrative is aspirational, above it real bid enters the token.
insights.quote: all of them require the USD SUSD APY to be above 6%

insights.claim: Total open interest in non-crypto markets — RWAs and equities — will eventually eclipse crypto open interest, and because there is always a bull market somewhere (AI equities in the first half of the year), an equity-perp basis sleeve is structurally more constructive for hitting Ethena's 6% threshold than crypto basis alone.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: The long-run bull case for Ethena is diversification of its basis sleeve away from crypto seasonality — but the RWA perp markets need years to reach the size its balance sheet requires.

insights.claim: Management-guided, programmatic buyback parameters are preferable to indiscriminate same-day-every-month buybacks, though a 6% yield and $7.5 billion trigger may only be attainable inside a bull market — meaning the protocol ends up buying its token back at higher prices.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Highlights the pro-cyclicality flaw in yield-gated buybacks — a design critique applicable to any protocol tying buybacks to performance thresholds.

insights.claim: Kunal's early-June ENA report called the tokenomics change, institutional lending, Coinbase as a driver, ENA's emergence as a yield creator (now visible in the Aladdin integration) and the RWA shift — and the token is up roughly 100% in the three months since.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A track-record datapoint on the panel's ENA framework, and a pointer to which of those called catalysts (institutional lending, RWA shift) still have runway.

themes.theme: DAT revival and the next catalysts

insights.claim: The USDe digital asset treasury was one of the worst-performing DATs in the drawdown but has rallied roughly 450% off its lows and was still trading at a discount to net asset value at last check — a case study showing DATs delivered strong upside beta to the underlying.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Discounted DATs on quality underlyings behave as leveraged recovery vehicles — a screenable setup if the rally persists.

insights.claim: If the market keeps grinding higher, select DATs will trade back above mNAV and restart the ATM issuance flywheel that fuels an explosive rally — but roughly 80% of DATs are simply not biddable, so the opportunity is confined to the one or two credible vehicles per underlying asset.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Frames a concentrated DAT trade — screen for the single best vehicle per asset trading near 1x mNAV rather than the sector.
insights.quote: if the market keeps rallying, a lot of these debts are going to be above MNAV again

insights.claim: Bitcoin and ETH DAT mNAVs on an enterprise-value basis set their floor over the summer and are just about to eclipse 1x, but a healthier premium than that is required before the ATM printer restarts and these vehicles resume bidding the underlying into year end.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: A specific, observable trigger level — mNAV meaningfully above 1x — that would bring a sidelined marginal buyer back into BTC and ETH.

insights.claim: The most underappreciated question in the market is whether Robin Hood chain plus FOMO can onboard genuinely new retail users and return onchain activity to 2023 levels, because the industry's pendulum has swung so far toward institutions and corporations that the retail growth story has been forgotten.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: The retail-revival thesis is the panel's highest-conviction underpriced narrative; the metrics to track are Robin Hood chain and FOMO user growth, not price.
insights.quote: the pendulum in crypto has swung so far towards the institutions and institutional use cases

insights.claim: Robin Hood chain and FOMO are growing the pie rather than cannibalizing incumbents — Pump Fun revenues are still rising alongside them — so competing venues should be rooting for their success on the logic that 10% of 10 million users beats 50% of 100,000.
insights.speaker: Ryan (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: Argues the retail-app trade is not zero-sum, supporting simultaneous long exposure across memecoin venues rather than picking one winner.
insights.quote: it's much better to have 10% of 10 million users versus 50% of 100,000 users

insights.claim: DTCC's October launch of tokenized assets is the key test of whether incumbent tokenized entitlements riding existing distribution beat the true onchain-equities model that Robin Hood and others are pursuing, with programmability and liquidity as the differentiators.
insights.speaker: Mark (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A dated, binary catalyst for the tokenization thesis — the outcome determines whether value accrues to incumbent infrastructure or to onchain venues.
insights.quote: I'm looking forward to the DTCC October launch of tokenized assets

insights.claim: ARC launches on mainnet around September 16 with FOMO confirmed live on day one, signalling that new chains now deliberately run the memecoin-trenches playbook to bootstrap liquidity, users and stress-testing before legitimate use cases arrive — though ARC lacks Robin Hood's distribution edge.
insights.speaker: Kunal (Blockworks research)
insights.so_what: A near-dated event where profits made on Robin Hood chain could rotate; the memecoin-bootstrap playbook is now a repeatable launch template to anticipate on every new chain.
insights.quote: Arc is launching on mainet on like September 16th
